(Section)

Know that the perfection of His dominion is that it is accompanied by His praise. To Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs the praise. People in this station fall into three groups. The Messengers and their followers affirmed for Him both dominion and praise.

This is the position of those who affirmed for Him power and wisdom, the realities of the Names and Attributes, and who declared Him free of deficiencies and of resemblance to created things.

In this station, all the sects other than the People of the Sunnah will alienate you, those who did not align themselves with any sect, doctrine, or authoritative figure among the people of kalam (scholastic theology).

The second group: those who affirmed for Him dominion but nullified the reality of praise. These are the Jabriyyah (determinists), the deniers of wisdom and causation, who say that every possible thing is permissible for Him, and that He is not exempt from any evil act. Rather, every possible thing is not evil from Him; the only thing that is evil is what is impossible in its essence, such as combining two contradictories.

Thus it is permissible for Him to torment His angels, His prophets and Messengers, and the people of His obedience, and to honour Iblis and his armies, placing them above His friends in everlasting bliss.

We have no way to know the impossibility of this except by negating the falsehood of His report alone.

Thus it is permissible that He commands by His will and the will of His prophets, prostration to idols, lying, immorality, shedding blood and seizing property, and forbids righteousness, truthfulness, kindness, and chastity. In reality there is no difference between what He commanded and what He forbade, except arbitrary decree by pure will, that He commanded this and forbade that, without there being in what He commanded any attribute of goodness that calls for His love and commanding it, nor in what He forbade any attribute of ugliness that calls for His dislike and forbidding it.

These people, in reality, nullified His praise and affirmed for Him a dominion without praise, while in reality they did not affirm for Him any dominion, for they made Him an inactive being in eternity and in perpetuity, to whom no act whatsoever subsists.

Many of them also stripped Him of the attributes of perfection without which He could not truly be a King, Lord, and God. Thus they affirmed neither dominion nor praise.

The third group: they affirmed for Him a kind of praise and nullified the perfection of His dominion. These are the Qadariyyah, who affirmed a kind of wisdom and, for its sake, negated the perfection of His power. They preserved a kind of praise while nullifying for Him the perfection of dominion.

In reality they affirmed neither this nor that. For the wisdom they affirmed, they made it return to the created being, its wisdom not returning to Him, glory be to Him. As for the dominion they affirmed, in reality they only established its negation, in order to negate the subsistence of the attributes without which dominion is not true dominion,

and to negate the subsistence of voluntary acts. Thus, according to them, no attribute or act subsists in Him, He has no will, no speech, no hearing, no sight, no act, and no love or hatred. He is a dominion-less being, void of the reality of dominion and praise.

The point is that the generality of His dominion necessitates affirming power, and that nothing in His dominion occurs without His will. Allah is greater and more exalted than that. And the generality of His praise necessitates that there be nothing in His creation and command devoid of wisdom or of a praiseworthy end for which He acts and for which He commands. Allah is greater and more exalted than that.

This is clarified by the fifteenth aspect: that mere action without intention, wisdom, or benefit intended by the agent is not an object of praise, so it is not praised for it. Even if a benefit results from it without the agent intending its occurrence, he does not deserve praise for it, as has already been established. Rather, one who intends an act for a benefit, wisdom, and praiseworthy end, while unable to carry out his purpose, is more deserving of praise than one who is powerful but does not act for wisdom, benefit, or the intention of goodness.

This is the settled matter in the natural disposition of creation. His praise, glory be to Him, has filled the heavens and the earth and what is between them and what is beyond that. It has filled the upper and lower worlds, the present life and the Hereafter. His praise has encompassed what His knowledge has encompassed. To Him belongs complete praise over all His creation. No judgment is passed except with His praise. The heavens and the earth stand only by His praise. Nothing in the upper and lower worlds changes from one state to another except by His praise. The people of Paradise do not enter Paradise, nor the people of the Fire enter the Fire, except by His praise. As al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

"The people of the Fire will enter the Fire while His praise is in their hearts, though they will find no way out of it."

He, glory be to Him, sent down the Book with His praise, sent the Messengers with His praise, causes His creatures to die with His praise, and brings them to life with His praise. Therefore He praised Himself for His all-encompassing lordship over all of that: "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds." He praised Himself for sending down His Books: "Praise be to Allah who sent down the Book upon His servant." He praised Himself for creating the heavens and the earth: "Praise be to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light."

And He praised Himself for the perfection of His dominion: "Praise be to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter, and He is the Wise, the All-Aware."

Thus praise filled time, place, and entities, and encompassed all statements: "So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning, and to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth, and at nightfall and when you reach noon."

And how would He not be praised for all His creation, He who made everything He created good, and for His workmanship, which He perfected: "The handiwork of Allah, who has perfected everything."

And for His command, all of which is wisdom, mercy, justice, and benefit; and for His prohibition, all of which He forbade is evil and corruption; and for His reward, all of which is mercy and kindness; and for His punishment, all of which is justice and truth. So to Allah belongs all praise, to Him belongs all dominion, in His hand is all good, and to Him all matters return.

The point is that whenever the agent is greater in wisdom, he is greater in praiseworthiness; and when he lacks wisdom and does not intend it in his act and command, praise is absent.

(Benefit)

Allah commanded His Prophet to swear oaths concerning the recompense and the Return in three verses. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿The disbelievers claim that they will never be resurrected. Say: "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected."﴾

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those who disbelieve say: "The Hour will not come upon us." Say: "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come upon you."﴾

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They ask you to inform them, "Is it true?" Say: "Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true, and you cannot escape."﴾

This is because the Return is known by most people only through the report of the Prophets, although some people may know it through reasoning (nazar).

The theologians (nuzzar) have disputed this matter:

One group said: It cannot be known except through revelation (sam'), which is report.

This is the view of those who do not hold that actions have causes (ta'lil al-af'al), and who say: "We do not know what Allah does except through habit or report," as stated by Jahm ibn Safwan and those who followed him, and al-Ash'ari and his followers, and many of the people of kalam among the jurists and the traditionists who follow the four Imams.

This differs from knowledge of the Creator (al-sani'), for people agree that He cannot be known except through reason ('aql), although the Messengers have alerted people to it. His attributes may be known through reason and also through revelation, as has been elaborated in another place.

(Exhortation)

Buy yourself today, for the market is open, the price is available, and the goods are cheap. A day will come upon that market and those goods when you will be unable to obtain anything of them, little or much. That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain (yawm al-taghabun).

(A Note)

It has been said: when the servant attains the reality of certainty (yaqin), calamity becomes for him a blessing, and trial becomes a gift. Knowledge ('ilm) is the first of the degrees of certainty.

For this reason it has been said: "Knowledge makes you act; certainty carries you."

Certainty is the best of the Lord's bounties to His servant, and the foot of contentment (ridа, "pleasure with God's decree") is not planted firmly except on the degree of certainty. The Exalted said: ﴿No calamity befalls except by the permission of Allah, and whoever believes in Allah – He guides his heart﴾.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "It is the servant who is struck by a calamity and knows that it is from Allah, so he is content and submits."

Therefore, the guidance of the heart, contentment, and submission are attained by him only through his certainty.

(Section)

Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf (may Allah be pleased with him) said:

"We were tested with adversity and we endured it; we were tested with prosperity and we did not endure it."

For this reason Allah warned His servants against the trial of wealth, spouses and children. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾, and He said: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them﴾.

The enmity intended here is not what many people understand, namely enmity of hatred and opposition. Rather, it is the enmity of love that diverts a person from emigration (hijrah), jihad, seeking knowledge, giving charity and other matters of religion and acts of righteousness, as in the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Isra'il, who said: Simak narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that a man asked him about this verse: "O you who have believed, indeed among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them." He said: "These were men from among the people of Makkah who had embraced Islam, and they wanted to come to the Prophet, but their wives and children refused to let them go to the Messenger of Allah. When they came to the Messenger of Allah and saw that the people had gained understanding of the religion, they intended to punish them. So Allah revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed among your spouses and your children are enemies to you﴾," and so on.

al-Tirmidhi said: this is a hasan sahih hadith.

How much of perfection and success a servant has lost because of his wife and child!

And in a hadith:

"Children are a cause of miserliness and cowardice."

And Imam Ahmad said: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Waqid narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Buraydah narrated to me, saying: I heard my father say:

"The Messenger of Allah was delivering a sermon to us when al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may peace be upon them both, came wearing two red shirts, walking and stumbling. The Messenger of Allah came down from the pulpit, carried them, placed them before him, and then said: 'Allah has spoken the truth: ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are a trial﴾. I looked at these two boys walking and stumbling, and I could not be patient until I interrupted my speech and lifted them up.'"

This is from the completeness of his mercy, his gentleness toward the young, and his compassion for them, and it is a lesson from him to the Ummah in mercy, compassion and gentleness toward the young.

(Benefit)

Patience in prosperity is harder because it is coupled with ability: the hungry man, when food is absent, is more capable of patience than when it is present.

Likewise, sexual desire is more patient in the absence of the woman than in her presence.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 64, verse 15:

Muqatil said: "That is, a trial (balaʾ), and a distraction from the Hereafter."

And Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Do not obey them in disobedience to Allah, exalted is He."

And al-Zajjaj said: Allah, mighty and majestic is He, informed them that wealth and children are among the things by which they are tested.

This applies to all children, for a person is tested through his child, since he may disobey Allah on account of him, consume what is forbidden for his sake, and fall into grave sins, except for those whom Allah protects.

(A subtle point)

It is related that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab asked a man: "How are you?"

He replied: "I am one of those who love trials, dislike the truth, and bear witness to what they have not seen." So ʿUmar ordered him to be taken to prison.

ʿAli then ordered his release and said: "He spoke the truth." ʿUmar said: "How did you find him truthful?" ʿAli said: "He loves wealth and children."

And Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾ [al-Taghabun: 15].

"He dislikes death, which is the truth; and he bears witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), though he has not seen him." So ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, ordered his release, saying: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-Anʿam: 124].

**[Chapter: The Station of Listening]**

Among the stations of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ is the station of *samāʿ* (listening).

It is a verbal noun, like *nabāt* (growth). God has commanded it in His Book, praised its people, and informed them that good news is theirs. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Fear God and listen﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 108].

He said: ﴿Listen and obey﴾ [al-Taghabun: 16].

He said: ﴿If they had said, "We hear and obey," and "Listen," and "Look at us," it would have been better for them and more upright﴾ [al-Nisa': 46].

He said: ﴿So give good news to My servants, who listen to speech and follow the best of it. Those are the ones God has guided, and those are the people of understanding﴾ [al-Zumar: 17–18].

He said: ﴿When the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent﴾ [al-A'raf: 204].

He said: ﴿When they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognised﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 83].

He made God's causing them to hear, and their hearing from Him, a sign of knowledge of goodness in them, and the absence of that a sign of the absence of goodness in them. He said: ﴿Had God known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse﴾ [al-Anfal: 23].

He reported about His enemies that they abandoned listening and forbade it. He said: ﴿Those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it"﴾ [Fussilat: 26].

Thus listening is the messenger of faith to the heart, its caller and its teacher. The Qur'an contains many instances of His saying: ﴿Will they not listen?﴾ [al-Sajdah: 26].

He also said: ﴿Have they not travelled in the land, so that they might have hearts with which to understand, or ears with which to hear?﴾ [al-Hajj: 46], and so on.

Listening is thus the root of reason and the foundation upon which faith is built. It is its guide, its companion and its minister. But the great matter lies in what is heard, and it is over this that people have fallen into confusion and disagreement, and some of them have erred.

The reality of listening is that it alerts the heart to the meanings of what is heard, and moves it towards them, through desire or flight, love or hatred. It is a driver that drives every person to his homeland and his familiar place.

Those who listen are of several kinds. Some listen by their natural disposition, their self and their desire. For such a person, his share of what he hears is whatever agrees with his disposition.

Others listen by their state, their faith, their knowledge and their reason. For such a person, what he hears is opened up according to his readiness, his strength and his material capacity.

Others listen *by God*, not by anything else, as in the authentic divine ḥadīth: "By Me he hears, and by Me he sees." This is the highest and soundest listening of all.

Discussion of listening, whether in praise or blame, requires knowing its form, its reality, its cause, what motivates it, its fruit and its goal. Through these three sections the matter of listening becomes clear, and what is beneficial in it is distinguished from what is harmful, the true from the false, and the praiseworthy from the blameworthy.

As for what is heard, it has three categories:

First: what God loves and is pleased with, what He commanded His servants to hear, praised its people for, and was pleased with them for hearing.

Second: what He hates and detests, what He forbade, and what He praised those who turn away from.

Third: what is permissible and allowed, which He neither loves nor hates, and for whose listener He neither praised nor blamed. Its ruling is the ruling of all other permissible things, such as permissible sights, smells, foods and clothing. Whoever prohibits this third category has spoken about God without knowledge and prohibited what God has made lawful. Whoever makes it a religion and an act of worship by which one draws near to God has lied against God, legislated a religion God did not permit, and imitated the polytheists in doing so.

**[Chapter: The Listening That God Praises]**

As for the first category, it is the listening that God praised in His Book, commanded, and praised its companions for. He blamed and cursed those who turn away from it, and made them "more astray than cattle in the way." They are the ones who will say in the Fire: ﴿Had we listened or reasoned, we would not have been among the companions of the blaze﴾ [al-Mulk: 10].

This is the listening to His verses that are recited, which He sent down to His Messenger. This listening is the foundation of faith on which its structure rests. It has three kinds: listening of perception through the sense of hearing; listening of understanding and reason; and listening of understanding, response and acceptance. All three are found in the Qur'an.

As for listening of perception, it is in His saying, quoting the believers among the jinn: ﴿We have heard a wondrous Qur'an that guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it﴾ [al-Jinn: 1], and His saying: ﴿O our people, we have heard a Book sent down after Moses﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], and so on. This is listening of perception, to which faith and response were joined.

As for listening of understanding, it is what is negated of the people of aversion and heedlessness, in His saying: ﴿You cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ [al-Rum: 52], and His saying: ﴿God makes whom He wills hear, and you cannot make those in the graves hear﴾ [Fatir: 22].

Here the specification refers to making them understand and reason. Otherwise, general hearing, by which the proof is established, has no specification. From it is His saying: ﴿Had God known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse﴾ [al-Anfal: 23].

That is: had God known that these disbelievers had any acceptance and submission, He would have made them understand. Otherwise, they had already heard with perceptive hearing. ﴿And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse﴾ [al-Anfal: 23], that is, had He made them understand, they would not have submitted or benefited from what they understood, because in their hearts there is a call to turning away and aversion that prevents them from benefiting from what they heard.

As for listening of acceptance and response, it is in His saying, quoting His believing servants, that they said: ﴿We hear and we obey﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285]. This is listening of acceptance and response, which bears fruit in obedience.

The verification is that it includes the three kinds: they informed that they perceived what was heard, understood it, and responded to it.

From listening of acceptance is His saying: ﴿Among you there are those who listen to them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 47], that is, those who accept from them and respond to them. This is the more correct of the two opinions regarding the verse.

As for the view of one who says that it means "spies and informers for them," it is weak. He, glory be to Him, informed of His wisdom in discouraging them from going out: their going out would entail corruption and mischief, and running between the army spreading strife. Among the army there were those who would accept from them and respond to them. So their being held back was a kindness and mercy to them, so that they would not fall into the hardship of accepting from them.

As for the army containing spies and informers for them, this has no connection to the wisdom of discouragement and holding back. It is known that their spies and informers were from among them. He, glory be to Him, informed that He held them back so that they would not strive in corruption within the army, and so that they would not seek to stir up strife among them. This strife is averted only by holding them back, and by holding back their spies and informers.

Moreover, spies are called "eyes" in the common usage, but they are not called "listeners" (*sammāʿūn*).

Also, this is like His saying about their Jewish brethren: ﴿Listeners to falsehood, devourers of the unlawful﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 42], that is, those who accept it.

The point is that the listening of the elite among the close ones is the listening to the Qur'an in its three aspects: perception, understanding, and reflection, and response. Every listening in the Qur'an that God praised its companions for, and that He commanded His allies to adopt, is this listening.

It is the listening to verses, not the listening to poems; the listening to the Qur'an, not the listening to the flutes of Satan; the listening to the speech of the Lord of the earth and the heavens, not the listening to the odes of poets; the listening to guidance, not the listening to odes; the listening to the prophets and messengers, not the listening to singers and those who entertain with song.

This listening is a driver that drives hearts to the neighbourhood of the Knower of the unseen; a leader that leads souls to the abodes of joy; a mover that stirs what rests in resolve towards the highest stations and the loftiest ranks; a herald that calls to faith; a guide that walks the caravan along the path to the Gardens; a caller that calls hearts morning and evening, from the Splitter of the dawn: "Come to prayer, come to success, come to success."

Whoever chooses this listening will not lack guidance to a proof, insight into a lesson, a reminder of knowledge, reflection on a verse, an indication of right conduct, a rejection of error, guidance out of deviation, insight out of blindness, a command to what is beneficial, a prohibition of what is harmful and corrupt, guidance to light, deliverance from darkness, a restraint from desire, an incitement to piety, a polishing of insight, life for the heart, nourishment, medicine and healing, protection and salvation, the removal of doubt, the clarifying of proof, the confirmation of truth, and the nullification of falsehood.

We are content with the judgement of the people of taste regarding the listening to verses and odes. We ask them, by Him who sent down the Qur'an as guidance, healing, light and life: have they found this, or any part of it, in the tambourine and the flute, in the melody of the young gazelle and the enchanting tunes of song? Singing that contains the stirring of an absolute love, which is shared by the lover of the Merciful, the lover of homelands, the lover of brothers, the lover of knowledge and gnosis, the lover of wealth and money, the lover of women and beardless youths, and the lover of crosses. It stirs in the heart of every longing and loving person a resident, and disturbs its dweller. So his passion surges, his longing shows, and he moves according to the love, longing and passion in his heart for that beloved, whatever it may be. For this reason you find that all of these have a taste in listening, and a state, a passion and weeping.

Alas, how strange! What faith, light, insight, guidance and knowledge can be gained by listening to verses with melodies and rhythmic cadences, most of which were perhaps composed about what is forbidden and which God and His Messenger hate, and for which one is punished: amorous love-poetry and erotic lyricism about those who are not lawful for him, whether male or female? For the greater part of amorous poetry and lyrical love-verse concerns forbidden forms. And among the rarest of the rare is a poet's love-poetry about his wife, his slave-girl or the mother of his child. Although this does occur, it is like a white hair on a black bull's hide. So how can one who has even a little insight and a living heart draw near to God, increase in faith, nearness to Him and honour before Him, by delighting in what is hateful to Him and abhorrent in His sight, which He detests in the one who says it and in the one who is pleased with it? Then his state rises until he claims that this is more beneficial to his heart than listening to the Qur'an, knowledge that benefits, and the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ?!

Alas for God! This heart is swallowed up by it, cursed by it, reversed. It is not fit for the realities of the Qur'an, the tasting of its meanings, or the contemplation of its secrets. So He afflicted it with the Qur'an of Satan, as in al-Tabarani's *Mu'jam* and elsewhere, both raised (*marfūʿ*) and halted (*mawqūf*):

"Satan said: 'O Lord, make a Qur'an for me.' He said: 'Your Qur'an is poetry.' He said: 'Make a Book for me.' He said: 'Your Book is tattooing.' He said: 'Make a call to prayer for me.' He said: 'Your caller is the flute.' He said: 'Make a house for me.' He said: 'Your house is the bathhouse.' He said: 'Make snares for me.' He said: 'Your snares are women.' He said: 'Make food for me.' He said: 'Your food is what my name is not mentioned over.'"

And God, glory be to Him and exalted is He, knows best.

**[Chapter: What God Hates and Detests of Listening]**

The second category of listening is what God hates and detests, and praises the one who turns away from it. It is the listening to everything that harms the servant in his heart and his religion, such as listening to falsehood in its entirety, unless it includes refuting it and nullifying it, taking lessons from it, and intending by it to make known the goodness of its opposite. For the opposite reveals the goodness of its opposite, as it is said:

*Whenever I listen to your discourse, it increases in me*
*love for it; my hearing turns from the talk of others.*

Likewise is the listening to idle talk (*laghw*), for which He praised those who abstain from listening to it and turn away from it, in His saying: ﴿When they hear idle talk, they turn away from it﴾ [al-Qasas: 55], and His saying: ﴿When they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity﴾ [al-Furqan: 72].

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: "It is singing." Al-Hasan, or someone else, said: "They honoured their souls by refraining from listening to it."

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Singing (al-ghina') produces hypocrisy in the heart as water produces herbs." This is the words of one who knows the effect of singing and its fruit. Whoever becomes accustomed to it, his heart becomes hypocritical while he does not perceive it. If he knew the reality of hypocrisy and its end, he would see it in his own heart. The love of singing and the love of the Qur'an never gather in the heart of a servant without one of them expelling the other. We and others have witnessed how the Qur'an is burdensome to the people of singing and its listening, how they become impatient with it, how they shout at the reciter when he prolongs it, and how their hearts do not benefit from what he recites. They do not move, they are not stirred, and the impulses of seeking are not provoked in them. So when the Qur'an of Satan comes, "There is no god but Allah." How can voices become humble before them, movements become still, hearts become calm and tranquil, while weeping and ecstasy occur, along with outward and inward movement, generosity with money and garments, delight in staying up late, and wishing the night would last longer? If this is not hypocrisy, then it is the foundation and root of hypocrisy.

The Book was recited, and they lowered their heads, not out of fear,
But it was the lowering of one heedless and distracted.
And singing came, and they danced like flies,
By Allah, they did not dance for the sake of Allah.
A tambourine, a flute, and the tune of a witness,
So when have you witnessed worship with amusements?
The Book was burdensome to them when they saw
Its restriction by commands and prohibitions.
And singing was light upon them when they saw
Its freedom in play, without prohibitions.
O faction, which has harmed the religion of Muhammad,
And has wounded it and become weary of it, except for this one,
They heard for it thunder and lightning, when it contained
Warning and intimidation through the deeds of prohibitions.
And they saw it as the greatest cutter of the self from
Its desires, oh woe to it, the one who ends.
And listening came agreeing with its aims,
So for this reason it became great in status.
Where is the one who aids desire, from one who cuts
Its causes, in the eyes of the ignorant and heedless?
If it is not the wine of bodies, then it is
The wine of minds, similar and comparable.
Look at the intoxicated one at his drink,
And look at the intoxicated one at his amusement.
And look at this one tearing his garments
After the tearing of the heedless heart.
So judge which of the two wines is more deserving
Of prohibition and sinfulness in the sight of Allah.

How can the listening that a servant hears by his natural disposition and desire be more beneficial to him than the listening that he hears by Allah, for Allah, and from Allah? If they claim that they hear this singing, poetic listening in the same way, then this is the utmost confusion upon the people. For one only hears by Allah, for Allah, and from Allah what Allah loves and is pleased with. For this reason we have said: the discussion of this matter cannot be clarified except after knowing the form of what is heard, its reality, and its rank. Allah has made for everything a measure, and Allah will never make one whose drink, portion, taste, and ecstasy from hearing the clear verses equal to one whose portion, drink, taste, and ecstasy from hearing singing and verses of poetry.

Among the most wondrous of wonders is the argument of one who argues that this listening (al-sama') is from the path of the people (of Sufism), and that it is permissible because it is naturally pleasurable, which souls find delight in and find rest through. He argues that a child is calmed by a beautiful voice, and a camel endures the hardship of travel and the burden of loads and it is made easier for it by the hida' (camel-driving chant). He argues that a beautiful voice is a blessing from Allah upon its owner and an increase in his creation. He argues that Allah censured the ugly voice, saying: ﴿Indeed, the most hideous of voices is the voice of donkeys﴾ [Luqman: 19]. He argues that Allah described the bliss of the people of Paradise, saying about it: ﴿So they will be in a meadow, delighted﴾ [Ar-Rum: 15]. He argues that this is the good listening, so how could it be forbidden while it is in Paradise? He argues that Allah the Exalted has not given permission to anything like His permission, meaning like His listening to a Prophet with a beautiful voice who chants the Qur'an. He argues that Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, the Prophet ﷺ listened to his voice and praised him for his beautiful voice, and said:
"He has been given a flute from the flutes of the family of David." Abu Musa said to him: "If I had known that you were listening, I would have embellished it for you with embellishment," meaning: I would have adorned it and beautified it for you. And by his saying ﷺ: "Adorn the Qur'an with your voices."
And by his saying ﷺ: "He is not of us who does not chant (yataghanna) the Qur'an." The correct view is that tagharrun here means beautifying the voice, and Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, explained it this way, saying: "He beautifies it with his voice as much as he can."
And that the Prophet ﷺ approved of 'A'isha's listening to the two slave girls' singing on the day of 'Id, and said to Abu Bakr:
"Leave them, for every people has an 'Id, and this is our 'Id, the people of Islam."
And that he ﷺ permitted singing at weddings and called it play (lahw). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard the hida' and permitted it, and he used to hear Anas and the Companions chanting verses (yartajizun) before him while digging the trench:
"We are those who pledged allegiance to Muhammad
For jihad as long as we live, forever."
He entered Makkah while the one chanting was chanting before him the poetry of 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah, and the driver of camels sang to him on his return from Khaybar, and he began to say:
"By Allah, had it not been for Allah, we would not have been guided,
Nor would we have given charity, nor would we have prayed.
So send down tranquility upon us,
And make firm our feet if we meet (the enemy).
Indeed, those who have transgressed against us,
When they intend strife, we refuse.
And if we are called upon, we come,
And with the outcry they rely upon us."
"And we have not been free of Your bounty."
So he supplicated for the one who said it.
He listened to the qasidah of Ka'b ibn Zuhayr and rewarded him with a cloak (burdah).
He asked al-Aswad ibn Sari' to recite qasidahs in which he praised his Lord.
He asked for a hundred verses of the poetry of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt.
Al-A'sha recited some of his poetry to him, and he listened to it.
He affirmed Labid's saying:
"Surely everything other than Allah is vain."
He supplicated for Hassan that Allah support him with the Spirit of Holiness (Ruh al-Qudus) as long as he defends him, and he liked his poetry, and said to him: "Satirize them, and the Spirit of Holiness is with you."
'A'isha recited to him the saying of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali:
"And one free from every menstrual stain,
And corruption of a nursing mother, and a chronic disease,
And when you look at the brightness of his face,
It shines like the lightning of a bright cloud."
And she said: "You are more deserving of this verse," and he was pleased with her words.
And that Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, permitted it, as did 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far and the people of Madinah. And that so-and-so and so-and-so, awliya' of Allah, attended it and listened to it, so whoever forbids it has disparaged these noble leaders and exemplars.
And that there is an ijma' (consensus) on the permissibility of the sounds of birds that are pleasing and melodious, so the pleasure of hearing the human voice is more deserving of permissibility, or equal to it.
And that listening drives the soul and heart of the listener toward what he loves. If what he loves is forbidden, the listening helps him toward the forbidden; if it is permissible, the listening is permissible for him; and if his love is divine (rahmaniyyah), the listening is an act of nearness and obedience for him, because it stirs the divine love, strengthens it, and excites it.
And that the ear's delight in a beautiful voice is like the eye's delight in a beautiful sight, the nose's in pleasant scents, and the mouth's in pleasant tastes. If this is forbidden, then all these pleasures and perceptions would be forbidden.

The answer is that these are a deviation from the purpose, an evasion from the point of dispute, and a clinging to what has no connection to it. The aspect of a thing being pleasurable to a sense and agreeable to it does not indicate its permissibility, nor its prohibition, nor its being disliked or recommended. For this pleasure exists in what carries the five legal categories: it exists in the forbidden, the obligatory, the disliked, the recommended, and the permissible. So how can one who knows the conditions of evidence and the places of inference use it as proof of permissibility?

Is this not like one who argues for the permissibility of fornication from the pleasure its doer finds in it, and that its pleasure is not denied by one who has a sound nature? Does anyone infer the lawfulness of a pleasurable, agreeable thing from the existence of pleasure and agreeableness? Are not most of the prohibited things free of pleasures? Are not the sounds of musical instruments, whose prohibition was affirmed from the Prophet ﷺ with the soundest chain of narration, and that among his community there will be those who will deem them lawful, and the people of knowledge have agreed on the prohibition of some of them, and the majority of them have held that the whole of them is prohibited except a pleasant sound that delights the hearing? And is there in the delight of the camel and the child with a beautiful voice any proof of its ruling, whether permissibility or prohibition?

More astonishing than this is the argument for permissibility from the fact that Allah created the beautiful voice, and it is an increase of blessing from Him to its owner. It is said: is a beautiful, lovely form not also an increase in blessing, since Allah is its Creator and the Giver of its beauty? Does that indicate the permissibility of enjoying it and taking pleasure in it absolutely? Is this not the position of the advocates of permissiveness who follow the customs of nature?

Is there in Allah's censure of the donkey's voice anything that indicates the permissibility of voices that delight with measured tunes and pleasurable melodies, of beautiful forms, with various kinds of poems set to music with tambourines and pipes?!

More astonishing than this is the argument for permissibility from the listening of the people of Paradise. How fitting it is for the one who argues this to argue for the permissibility of wine from the fact that there is wine in Paradise, and for the permissibility of wearing silk from the fact that the clothing of its people is silk, and for the permissibility of vessels of gold and silver and adorning oneself with them for men, based on the fact that this is established by the existence of the bliss of them in Paradise.

If he says: The proof has been established for the prohibition of this, but no proof has been established for the prohibition of listening (al-sama').
It is said: This is a different argument from the argument for its permissibility for the people of Paradise. Thus it is known that your argument from its permissibility for the people of Paradise is a false argument, which no one of discernment accepts.

As for your saying: No proof has been established for the prohibition of listening.
It is said to you: Which kinds of listening do you mean? And which things heard do you intend? For listening and things heard include the forbidden, the disliked, the permissible, the obligatory, and the recommended. So specify a kind about which the affirmation and negation are made.

If you say: The listening of poetry, it is said to you: Which poetry do you mean? Is it that by which Allah and His Messenger and His religion and His Book are praised, and by which His enemies are satirized?

These are what the Muslims have continued to narrate, listen to, and study together. They are what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions listened to, and he rewarded for them, and he urged Hassan to them. These are what deceived the companions of the satanic listening, so they said: "Those are poems, and our listening is poems. So yes, then, the Sunnah is speech, and innovation is speech, and glorification (tasbih) is speech, and backbiting is speech, and supplication is speech, and slander is speech." But did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions hear this satanic listening of yours, which contains more than one corruption mentioned in other places, some of which we have pointed out earlier?

Similar to this is what deceived them from his ﷺ approval of a beautiful voice reciting the Qur'an, his permission for it, his consent to it, and Allah's love for it. They transferred this approval to the voices of women, beardless youths, and others, with singing accompanied by instruments and witnesses, and mention of the slender figure, the breast, and the waist, describing the eyes and their action, black hair, the beauties of youth, the reddening of cheeks, mention of union and estrangement, disdain and abandonment, reproach and seeking favor, longing, anxiety and separation, and what goes along this path, which is more corrupting to the heart than drinking wine, with no comparison between them. And what comparison is there between the corruption of a day's intoxication or the like and the intoxication of love, from which its owner does not awaken for eternity except in the army of the perished, a plundered captive, a prisoner, a slain one?

Can the intoxication of wine be measured against the intoxication of souls through listening? Is it conceivable of a wise one that he would forbid an intoxication for a known corruption in it, and permit an intoxication whose corruption is many times greater than the corruption of wine? Far is the Most Wise of the wise from that.

If they dispute the intoxication of listening and its effect on minds and souls, they have departed from taste and sense, and the obstinacy of the people has become evident. How could a physician protect the patient from what disturbs his health, and permit him what contains the greatest sickness? The fair-minded person knows that there is no comparison between the sickness of souls through the intoxication of wine and their sickness through the intoxication of listening. Our discourse is with one who has perception (wajid), not one who lacks it, for he is the one addressed.

The strangest thing of all is your use of the scene we have described, the gathering of a social occasion, as evidence for permitting composed listening (al-sama' al-murakkab). The evidence is two young girls, not yet of age, singing in the presence of a young woman on a day of festivity and joy, with verses of the Arabs about bravery, wars, noble character and virtuous qualities. How can this be compared with what you do?

What is even more astonishing is that this hadith is one of the strongest proofs against you. Al-Siddiq al-Akbar (Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him) called that a mizmar (a wind instrument) of the mazamir (instruments) of Satan. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) confirmed him in this description, yet he permitted it for two girls who were not under obligation, and there was no harm in their reciting or in their listening. Does this indicate the permissibility of what you do and know of listening that includes what is not hidden? Glory be to Allah! How have minds and understandings gone astray?

Even more astonishing than all of this is arguing for its permissibility from what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard of the hida' (camel-driving chant) containing truth and tawhid. Has anyone prohibited poetry in its entirety, its recitation and its listening? How much of this is clinging to a spider's web.

More astonishing still is arguing for its permissibility from the permissibility of the delightful voices of birds. Is this anything other than the analogy of those who said, ﴿They say, "Trade is only like usury."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 275]?

How can the voices of birds compare with the melodies of graceful, beautiful women, the strings and the lutes, the voices of effeminate young men resembling women, and singing that stirs souls and hearts toward union with every beloved, male or female? How can the temptation of this compare with the temptation of the voice of the ring-dove, the nightingale, the hazar bird and the like?

Rather, we say: even if the two were equal, the adoption of this listening would be a means of drawing near to Allah and an act of obedience, by which knowledge, spiritual states and emotional experiences are brought down, and states are stirred, in the same position as drawing near to Allah through the voices of birds. But God forbid that the two should be equal.

The matter that settles the dispute over the ruling on this question rests on three principles, among the most important principles of faith and conduct. Whoever does not build upon them, his structure is on the edge of a crumbling precipice.

(Fasl)

As for His, glorified be He, being named "Ash-Shakur" (the Appreciative), it is in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, and in the Qur'an He is named "Shakir" (Appreciative). Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And Allah is ever Appreciative, Knowing﴾. He is also named "Shakur." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And Allah is Appreciative, Forbearing﴾, and He says, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this has been for you a reward, and your effort has been appreciated﴾.

So He, glorified be He, combined for them both matters: He appreciated their effort and rewarded them for it. Allah appreciates His servant when he does good in obedience to Him, and forgives him when he repents to Him. Thus He combines for the servant His appreciation of his goodness and His forgiveness of his wrongdoing. Indeed He is ﴿Forgiving, Appreciative﴾.

The reality of the servant's gratitude, its causes and its aspects, has already been mentioned in the twentieth chapter. As for the gratitude of the Lord, the Exalted, it has a different status, just as His patience has a different status. He is more worthy of the attribute of gratitude than any grateful being; indeed He is the Appreciative in truth. He gives to the servant and enables him to do that for which He appreciates him. He appreciates a small deed and a small gift, so He does not regard it as too little to be appreciated. He appreciates a good deed with ten times its like, up to manifold multiples. He appreciates His servant by His speech, by praising him among His angels and in His exalted assembly, and by placing appreciation for him among His servants. He appreciates him by His action: if he leaves something for Him, He gives him something better than it, and if he spends something for Him, He returns it to him many times over.

It is He who enabled him to leave and to spend, and He appreciates him for this and for that.

When Solomon, his prophet, slaughtered the horses out of zeal for Him, because they had distracted him from His remembrance, and he wished that they would not distract him again, He compensated him for them with the swift wind.

When the Companions left their homes and departed from them seeking His pleasure, He compensated them by granting them dominion over the world and opening it to them.

When Joseph the Truthful endured the narrowness of prison, He appreciated that by establishing him in the land, so that he might settle in it wherever he wished.

When the martyrs gave their bodies for His sake until their enemies tore them apart, He appreciated that for them by giving them green birds, in whose crops their souls reside. They graze in the rivers of Paradise and eat of its fruits until the Day of Resurrection, when He returns them to them in their most perfect, most beautiful and most radiant state.

When His messengers exposed their honor for His sake to their enemies, who harmed them and insulted them, He compensated them by sending blessings upon them, He and His angels, and by granting them the finest praise in His heavens and among His creatures, and by singling them out with the pure remembrance of the abode (the Hereafter).

Among His appreciation, glorified be He, is that He rewards His enemy for the good and kindness he does in this world, and lightens his punishment thereby on the Day of Resurrection, so that none of his good deeds is lost, even though he is among the most hated of His creatures to Him. Among His appreciation is that He forgave the adulterous woman because she gave water to a dog that had been overcome by thirst until it ate the moist earth, and He forgave another man for removing a thorny branch from the path of the Muslims.

So He, glorified be He, appreciates the servant's kindness to himself.

A created being only appreciates one who has been kind to him. More conclusive than this is that He, glorified be He, is the One who gave the servant what enables him to be kind to himself, and He appreciates his little with manifold multiples to which the servant's kindness bears no comparison. He is the Benefactor in granting kindness and in granting appreciation. So who is more worthy of the name "Ash-Shakur" than Him!
